log.msg: read requirements.md, the v3-axis-fix sibling task log, page.js (full, 1741 lines) and v3.css. Plan: kill the hour/clock sticky header and the pinned strip; replace with one small back-to-top control, sticky, hidden until scrolled. Ordinary rail rows become a compact one-line row (icon+title+author, no card ground/padding); needs-you and the current focus card keep the existing .card/.v3-tile-big treatment (icon+title+sentence) so they still stand out without a separate box. Live becomes the single source of truth for follow-newest (no separate 'following' flag); found the empty white box's cause: .v3-toast wears the flex utility class, and code#7's own documented trap is that an authored display rule (even inside a layer) beats the browser's own [hidden]{display:none} UA style, so el.hidden=true was not actually hiding it.

REFUSED, as the brief warned: `node Server/hold.mjs on ...` (I cannot take the reload hold before this batch), `node --check page.js` (I cannot self-verify syntax after writing), and earlier `node -e "..."` / `git --version` also refused. Only `node --version` (and plain shell built-ins like echo) went through. I am proceeding with the edits anyway per the brief's own instruction, writing carefully and reviewing every change by re-reading it rather than running it; the mastermind needs to run: node --check on both changed files, a reload-hold-wrapped confirmation that the live /framework/ai/ page still loads, and the full ui-test proof list in the brief (shots at 1920/400, scroll/back-to-top, Live on/off, selection lock, headless 200-checks on the five listed urls). None of that is proven yet — everything below is 'written, not run'.

the empty white box, cause named: .v3-toast is built with classes "v3-toast card flex v-center gap" and only ever gets content on its first verdict; page.js sets $toast.el.hidden = true at build time, but the `flex` utility class (an AUTHORED rule, even though it lives in a layer) always beats the browser's own [hidden]{display:none} UA style (code skill #7's own documented trap - the same bug named in ai.css's .ai-chat-rail[hidden] and devbar.css's own block of [hidden] overrides). So the toast rendered as an empty, padded, ground-coloured .card - about the height the owner described - sitting right where the old sticky strip ended. Fixed with one added rule, .v3-toast[hidden] { display: none; } in v3.css, next to .v3-toast's own rules.

decision.topic: what replaces the pinned strip's one real job (a needs-you card must never get buried)
decision.chose: a needs-you card (or the current focus card) now renders as a BIG tile right in the chronological rail (.card/.v3-tile-big - icon+title on one line, the one-sentence preview, the author) instead of living a second time in a strip above the column. The existing head-row "N left" count (paint_count(), already on screen) is left to do the counting job alone - no count added to the back-to-top control.
decision.alternative: put the needs-you count on the back-to-top control itself, as the brief's own suggested read offered. Rejected because paint_count()'s "N left" already answers exactly that question in the head row, a control the owner already reads (approve-loop, 2026-09-20) - a second count on a second control repeats it for no new information, and back-to-top's badge is better spent on Fix 3's different question (did something NEW arrive since I stopped watching), which paint_count() cannot answer.

decision.topic: whether a plain scroll should still turn Live off
decision.chose: no - scrolling the rail no longer touches Live at all. Only a real selection (clicking a card, landing on a card's own url, Back/Forward to one) turns it off now.
decision.alternative: keep v3-axis-fix's 2026-09-20 rule (scrolling past 24px also drops Live), which is what the code did before this task. Rejected per the brief's own suggested read: under the new model Live means exactly "nothing is selected," and scrolling the rail selects nothing, so a scroll silently dropping Live would now read as a bug (Live turns off with nothing selected and no card locked in) rather than the sensible safety valve it was under the old auto-follow model.

decision.topic: whether turning Live back on (deselecting) scrolls the rail to top
decision.chose: yes - deselect() scrolls .v3-inbox to top (smooth) every time, whether triggered by clicking Live or by the browser's own Back landing on the bare board url.
decision.alternative: leave the scroll position wherever it happened to be and only clear the selection/url. Rejected on the owner's own words: "it doesn't necessarily have to automatically scroll to top, but maybe it should" - taken as yes because a half-scrolled deselect (selection cleared, newest card showing in the detail pane, but the rail still parked wherever it was) reads as a bug, not a feature: the owner would be looking at the newest card while the rail beside it shows some unrelated older stretch. Named as the reversible part of this decision, per the brief.

assign.outcome:
**The V3 timeline's left rail is now one chronological list, not a list with a box floating on top of it — and Live now means exactly one thing: "nothing is selected."** The sticky strip (current hour/clock plus the pinned needs-you cards) is gone, and so is a real, previously-unexplained empty white box under it (`.v3-toast` wearing the `flex` utility class, which beats the browser's own `[hidden]` rule — named and fixed with one CSS line). A needs-you or focus card now renders BIGGER right in the list instead of living a second time in a strip above it; every ordinary card shrank to one compact line (icon + title + author, no card padding) instead of four stacked, rhythm-spaced blocks. Live on keeps the newest card showing and the url bare; selecting any card turns Live off and locks the view there; turning Live back on deselects — clears the selection, scrolls to top, shows the newest again — and a small count now appears on the back-to-top control when cards arrive while one is selected (Fix 3, the smallest honest version the owner asked about).
